stem.text: Consider the curve given by \( \left(y - 9\right)^{2} = 9\left(3 - x\right)^{2}\left(6 - x\right) \). The derivative is \( \frac{dy}{dx} = - \frac{27 \left(x - 5\right) \left(x - 3\right)}{2 y - 18} \). Find all points on the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal.

answer_key.label: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (5, 15) \) and \( (5, 3) \).

worked_solution.text: The numerator is zero where \( x = 3 \) or \( x = 5 \). At \( x = 3 \) the curve gives \( y = 9 \), where the denominator is also zero, so no horizontal tangent is decided there.
worked_solution.rule_named: numerator zero with a nonzero denominator

worked_solution.text: At \( x = 5 \) the relation gives \( \left(y - 9\right)^{2} = 36 \), so \( y = 15 \) or \( y = 3 \), and the denominator is not zero at either.
worked_solution.rule_named: solve the relation and the condition together

worked_solution.text: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (5, 15) \) and \( (5, 3) \).

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal only where \( x = 5 \).
options.derivation: the input x = 5 reported alone where points were asked for
